newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends down as trade, specs sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends down as trade, specs sell.

text.p: Trade and speculative selling pressured CSCE world sugar futures to close near the lows, but shortcovering held the most-active May contract over support seen at 10.85 cents, dealers said.
May ended down 0.20 cent at 10.90 cents, having ranged from 11.01 to 10.89 cent. Spot March settled 0.26 cent lower to 10.92, while the outer months finished down 0.16 to 0.09.
Volume was estimated at 27,280 lots compared with Friday's official volume of 42,776 lots.

"There was very good trade selling in March on the open which allowed prices to come in 20 points lower on liquidation before Friday," a broker said, referring to the last trading day for March sugar futures.
He said the speculators were the main sellers of the March/May spread, which narrowed to 0.02 cent from 0.08 cent Friday.
Market sources said today's close near the lows may signal additional losses Tuesday. A move under support basis May push prices into the 10.60-cent a lb range, they said.
Open interest in the May contract rose by 3,650 lots to 65,144 lots from Friday.
In Brazil, a warehouse workers strike at the key port of Santos is expected to have a greater impact on imports than exports, a spokeswoman said.
